text:
maria_customer: Hey team, since we onboarded aurora-v2 yesterday our API /v1/generate p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~2.3s for long-context requests (>12k tokens). No code changes on our end. Looks tied to tokenization changes? :frowning:

sara_support: Sorry you're seeing that — can you share a request id and sample payload? Are you using the hosted API or a Dedicated pool?

maria_customer: request id 0a9f3b-aurora-5178, hosted API in us-west. Example: POST /v1/generate with prompt length ~18k tokens, model=aurora-v2, max_tokens=512. Repro steps: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate

liam_infra: Noted. We're seeing a cluster-side pattern: continuous-batching interactions with the new tokenizer are producing more micro-batches (many small sequences) and causing serialization stalls around KV cache warmup. p99 correlates with batch count spikes.

jun_eng-runtime: Quick dump from the runtime during the spike:
```
[2026-03-15T22:12:03Z] model=aurora-v2 shard=3 batch_size=1 queued=32 wait=230ms decode=1850ms total=2125ms
[2026-03-15T22:12:04Z] tokenizer=aurora-v2-split mode=extended subtoken_count=1.8x expected=1.0x
[2026-03-15T22:12:04Z] kv_hit=false prefix_cache_miss=0.78
```
jun_eng-runtime: The tokenizer's new heuristics are producing more very-short subtokens for certain long-form inputs (multilingual + lots of punctuation), which inflates sequence counts and increases batching churn.

sara_support: Is there an immediate mitigation we can offer the customer?

liam_infra: Short term: force the onboarded model to the legacy tokenizer variant (aurora-v2-tokenizer-legacy) via model_variant pinning, or set header `X-Redwood-Tokenize: legacy` for affected requests. That should reduce microbatching. Also lowering `max_batch_size` from default 64 to 16 on the Dedicated pools helps, but not available for hosted unless we route.

maria_customer: Can you show the header approach? We need a quick patch.

sara_support: Example curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Tokenize: legacy" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"aurora-v2","input":"<very long prompt>","max_tokens":512}'
```

jun_eng-runtime: We're also rolling a runtime hotfix to improve subtoken coalescing and prioritize filling larger batches when sequence lengths are similar. ETA for canary is ~2 hours. It should reduce p99 by ~40% in our tests for similar traffic patterns.

liam_infra: Ops note: monitor batch queue depth + subtoken_rate metric. If subtoken_rate > 1.4 for >5m, auto-route new requests to aurora-v2-legacy until canary completes. I've added a temporary policy in the routing layer.

maria_customer: We see immediate improvement when adding the header, p99 back to ~480ms. Thanks. One more ask — our billing bumped because of retries during the spike, can support review credits?

sara_support: Filed a billing review ticket and tagged billing@ — ticket #BILL-2239. We'll include request id and time ranges.

ops-bot: Deploy started: runtime-hotfix-subtoken-coalesce canary -> 3 nodes (liam_infra approved)

liam_infra: After canary looks healthy, we'll do a staged rollout with a rollback window. I'll keep this thread updated.

jun_eng-runtime: Postmortem notes to follow: root cause = tokenizer heuristics causing subtoken fragmentation for long multilingual inputs + runtime batching heuristic not compensating for higher sequence counts. Mitigations = tokenizer fallback flag, runtime coalescing hotfix, routing policy, and a prompt-size guidance doc for customers.

maria_customer: Great, appreciate the fast help. We'll keep the legacy header in place until you confirm rollout is done. :thumbsup:

sara_support: Thanks all — keeping this open until rollout finishes and billing is resolved.
